requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 (and node2, needed for cross-node access)
requirements.summary: useradd -m created opsbot (uid 1000) on both node1 and node2, confirmed via id output.

requirements.requirement: opsbot on node1 has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: ed25519 keypair generated on node1, public key installed into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2 with correct permissions, and end-to-end SSH command execution (whoami/hostname/echo) as opsbot@node2 verified from node1 both before and after node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node1 (password auth disabled)
requirements.summary: A Match User opsbot sshd_config block enforcing PasswordAuthentication no / AuthenticationMethods publickey was added, validated with sshd -t, and reloaded; sshd -T confirms the effective policy is publickey-only for opsbot on node1, both before and after the node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node2 (password auth disabled)
requirements.summary: Same Match User block applied and reloaded on node2; sshd -T confirms publickey-only policy, and getent shadow shows opsbot's password hash locked with '!!' prefix, both before and after the node2 restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: opsbot was created on both nodes, key-based SSH access from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 was established and functionally verified (including after both nodes were restarted), and password authentication for opsbot was disabled and enforced via a Match User sshd_config block plus a locked password hash on node2, confirmed via sshd -T on both hosts. The provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly with clear pre-restart baselines, boot-id changes, and full post-restart recovery of sshd, the opsbot account, the key-only policy, and end-to-end SSH access on both node1 and node2. One minor, fully-reverted troubleshooting mutation (a temporary password set and then relocked on node2) is the only notable hygiene finding.
limitations: No evidence was captured of a login attempt using a password for opsbot to directly negative-test password rejection (e.g., ssh with a password or PasswordAuthentication client flag); the conclusion that password auth is blocked rests on sshd -T effective-config output and the locked shadow hash rather than an observed failed password login.

The temporary password set on node2 (cmd-46b597b1009f4ee7) was not evidenced as tested against a live SSH connection attempt to directly confirm it was rejected by the key-only policy, so its role appears to be a partial/incomplete verification effort rather than a completed check.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene is good: the sshd_config edits and account creation are minimal and directly tied to the task, syntax-validated before reload, and cross-verified after reboot. One unnecessary mutation is notable: cmd-46b597b1009f4ee7 set a temporary password ('opsbot:TempPass123!') for opsbot on node2 via chpasswd, seemingly as an ad hoc test of the policy; this was not required to satisfy the task (the Match block and locked hash already established key-only access) and briefly weakened the account's credential state. It was reverted immediately afterward by cmd-cf5446a0d2524fb8 (passwd -l), and the final getent shadow output (cmd-429de851f814493a) confirms the password hash is locked again, so the mutation was bounded and fully restored, not retained. The restart protocol left an expected /tmp/reboot.log artifact on both nodes from the backgrounded reboot command, which is low-risk residue directly tied to the restart evidence process rather than abandoned troubleshooting. No failed services, package-health issues, or unexpected listening sockets were introduced (after_executor comparison shows only boot-id, sshd PID, and reboot.log/systemd-private tmp dir churn, all expected from the two restarts).
